## d486b924dcdf

**Reproduced domain defect and shortcut.** Canonical `train[2]` has three nonzero key colors in row 0: `4`, `7`, and `2`. The target generator declares `n_keys=2..2`, always emits exactly two keys, and its `self_check` rejects that canonical input with `row 0 should have exactly 2 key-color cells; found 3`.

This creates a concrete generated-only shortcut: “use only the first two nonzero key colors.” It is indistinguishable from the authority on every generated example because generation never supplies a third key, but it drops the color-2 body object on canonical `train[2]`. `checks/audit/d486b924dcdf/validator_and_rival.json` contains the canonical input identity, validator error, rival output, generator hash `de3361262cf3822db23671390da05787481af211812732150216db589e3fd2e6`, and supported replay command. `checks/audit/d486b924dcdf/racket.json` confirms rule hash `a9e1e2c437e8` and returns the full three-key canonical output, which differs from the rival.

Suggested repair direction: make key count an exact observable axis covering at least 2–3, accept all canonical inputs, and require a linked lesson containing a three-key case. No audit-target files were changed.
